scope: SAMPLED spatial diagnostic:32 evenly spread GT-matched frames per indoor sequence;64frames total, not full-sequence spatial statistics

sampling.method: np.rint(np.linspace(0,M-1,32)).astype(int) over the source-ordered GT-matched frame list

mask.evaluation: joint GT and prediction valid; no clipping, maximum GT depth, crop or resizing

edge_definition.neighbors: 4-neighbor horizontal/vertical valid-GT pairs; mark both endpoints
edge_definition.invalid_gt_boundaries: not treated as a depth jump
edge_definition.outside_label: outside detected discontinuity band; not claimed planar/flat

aggregation: Pool valid sampled pixels separately within each sequence and region; AbsRel=sum(abs(pred-GT)/GT)/N; RMSE=sqrt(sum((pred-GT)^2)/N); signed error=pred-GT. Exact pooled median of signed errors stored as float32 for the median calculation. These are pixel-pooled metrics, unlike the dense evaluator frame-macro means.
limitations: GT-based discontinuity detection uses a chosen absolute/relative jump threshold and a7x7band; conclusions depend on these settings.
Depth-bin distributions and regional errors reflect64selected frames and their valid GT support, not every frame or all image pixels.
TUM has sensor holes and nearest-timestamp GT associations. Valid-pair edge detection does not interpret holes as depth edges.
No network inference, scale fitting, correction, cache changes or GT-driven model input was performed.
Outside the detected band does not mean geometrically flat. Thresholded spatial statistics alone do not establish semantic failure causes.

provenance.computation: one-off inline diagnostic; no project scripts modified
